rooms.name: Living / kitchen / entry
rooms.note: One tall room. Gear bay by the door, kitchenette on the north wall, stove and sofa in the middle, desk at the glass.

rooms.name: Bedroom 1
rooms.note: Queen platform bed with drawers. Sliding door. Egress casement on the east wall.

rooms.name: Bath + laundry
rooms.note: 34 x 36 in shower with 24 in clear in front, toilet, 18 in vanity. Washer-dryer, tankless water heater and the water manifold share the southeast corner.

site.slope: Gentle fall to the northeast (assumed). Snow and runoff go north and east, away from the entry.

general: These drawings are for planning and permit preparation. They are not for construction until reviewed and stamped by a licensed engineer and approved by the building department.
Design to the 2021 IRC and 2021 IECC unless the county has adopted a different year.
Verify all dimensions in the field. Dimensions are to the outside of framing unless noted.
The model, drawings and estimate come from one data file (model.json). Change the file, not the drawings.
foundation: Concrete 4,000 psi, air-entrained. Rebar ASTM A615 Grade 60.
Bottom of footings at least 48 in below grade or the county frost depth, whichever is deeper.
Piers: 12 in round (18 in under the covered-entry posts) with 4 #4 vertical bars, on footings sized from the loads. Shared pads and hold-down piers where marked on S-101.
Crawlspace: 20 x 10 in footing, 8 in stem wall, 1/2 in anchor bolts at 6 ft o.c., R-15 continuous insulation, sealed 12 mil vapor barrier, passive radon stack.
framing: Exterior walls 2x6 at 16 in o.c. LSL studs where walls are taller than 12 ft (spacing on S-301).
Floor: 11 7/8 in I-joists (TJI 210 or equal) at 16 in o.c. in hangers between flush 3-ply LVL beams. LVL end beams under the east and west walls.
Roof: 16 in rafters on beveled plates, tied at every bearing. Simple spans that break over the north wall and the garage south wall. Spacing by snow load.
South glass wall: steel tube posts (HSS 5 x 3) between the glass bays with wood bucks; LVL headers sit on welded seats.

Bedroom wing ceiling: 2x10 at 16 in o.c., hung from a 2-ply 2x10 flush header near the north wall where the rafters come down; short 2x10s between the rafters north of it. Strong enough for a storage loft.
Wind bracing: shear wall panels, hold-downs, collectors and roof deck nailing per S-401.
Wall sheathing ZIP System R-6 (R-6.6 foam), all seams taped. It is the air and water barrier.
envelope: Walls R-23 mineral wool plus R-6.6 continuous (ZIP System R-6). Roof about R-60: 16 in of dense-pack cellulose (see the roof check). Floor R-44 dense-pack cellulose (piers) or R-15 crawl walls (crawlspace).
Cold roof: a 3 1/2 in vent channel above the lower deck runs from the north soffit to the south soffit.
Air barrier: taped wall sheathing, taped lower roof deck, sealed subfloor. Target 3 air changes per hour at 50 Pa or better.
systems: No water lines in exterior walls. All supply and drain lines run in the insulated floor north of the middle beam.
Low-point drain valve at the water entry. Blow out lines and add RV antifreeze to traps before leaving the house unheated.
Bath fan runs all the time at 50 cfm. That is the whole-house fresh-air system.
Smoke alarms in each bedroom, combined smoke/CO alarms in the living room near each bedroom door, all hardwired and interconnected.
Keep the roof clear of anything that sliding snow could hit except the chimney, which gets a snow splitter.
